'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian conflict (2024–present)|Syrian conflict]]
**[[SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes (2025–present)|SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes]]
***[[2026 northeastern Syria offensive]]
****Heavy fighting occurs around [[Kobani]] between the [[Syrian Army]] and [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] (SDF) despite a [[ceasefire]] announced by both sides the previous day. Government forces capture the towns of [[Ayn Issa]] and [[Sarrin]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/1/19/syria-live-government-forces-take-control-after-heavy-fighting-with-sdf (Al Jazeera)]
****The SDF says it has lost control of a [[prison]] holding thousands of [[Islamic State]] (IS) fighters in the town of [[Al-Shaddadah]] after the prison came under attack from armed groups. A video released by the SDF appears to show dozens of IS militants [[prison escape|escaping the prison]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jan/19/kurdish-led-forces-clashes-syrian-army-prison-holding-is-inmates (''The Guardian'')] [https://hawarnews.com/en/sdf-shaddadi-prison-out-of-control (ANHA)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/kurdish-led-force-says-armed-group-attacks-syria-prison-holding-thousands-2026-01-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict (2022–present)|Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict]], [[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***[[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese troops]] and allied [[Wazalendo]] militia fighters re-enter [[Uvira]], [[South Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], after it had been held for about a month by the [[Rwanda]]-backed [[March 23 Movement]]. '''Health and environment'''
*[[Aging of China]], [[Aging of South Korea]]
**Reflecting a broader [[population ageing|demographic decline]] across [[East Asia]], the [[birth rate]] in [[China]] fell to 5.6 per 1,000 people last year, the lowest since records began in 1949, according to the [[Economist Intelligence Unit]], as similar downward trends persist in [[Singapore]], [[South Korea]], and [[Taiwan]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/19/china-birthrate-record-low-aging-population-fertility-crisis.html (CNBC)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c79r7v7qr53o (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Greenland crisis]]
**[[Operation Arctic Endurance]]
***[[Denmark]] announces that it will send "a substantial number" of [[Danish Defence|troops]] to [[Greenland]] in response to threats from [[United States]] [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/denmark-deploys-more-soldiers-to-greenland-reports/3803966 (AA)]
**[[NORAD]] announces that it will deploy [[United States|American]] and [[Canada|Canadian]] aircraft to [[Pituffik Space Base]] in Greenland for long-planned activities, describing the deployment as routine and coordinated with the Denmark with diplomatic clearances and with the [[Naalakkersuisut|Government of Greenland]] informed of the planned operations. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-sends-aircraft-to-greenland-base-amid-tensions-over-trumps-takeover-bid/3804555 (AA)] [https://taskandpurpose.com/news/norad-greenland-aircraft-routine/ (Task & Purpose)]
*[[Kiribati–New Zealand relations]]
**[[Kiribati]] and [[New Zealand]] sign a [[partnership agreement]] on economic opportunity, [[foreign policy]], health, and security, marking their first [[bilateral agreement]] since a diplomatic crisis began in 2025. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/new-zealand-kiribati-relationship-warms-with-partnership-agreement-2026-01-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Guatemala]] 
**A ninth policeman succumbs to his injuries from prison riots and attacks on [[National Civil Police (Guatemala)|police]] officers in [[Guatemala]]. A dozen officers were also injured in the attacks, and a [[state of emergency]] has been declared. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260119-ninth-policeman-dies-in-guatemala-gang-riots-attacks (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Flood control projects scandal in the Philippines]]
**Former [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Senator of the Philippines|senator]] [[Bong Revilla]] surrenders to [[Philippine National Police|police]] after the [[Sandiganbayan]] ordered his arrest over the alleged [[Corruption in the Philippines|misuse]] of [[Philippine peso|₱]]92.8 million (US$1.6 million) in a [[Flood management|flood-control]] project, while the [[Office of the Ombudsman (Philippines)|Ombudsman]] pursues [[Graft (politics)|graft]] and [[Malfeasance in office|malversation]] charges against Revilla and several former [[Department of Public Works and Highways|public works officials]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/philippines/former-senator-bong-revilla-surrenders-over-p928-million-flood-control-project-in-bulacan-1.500413684 (''Gulf News'')]
*[[September 2022 Burkina Faso coup d'état]]
**[[Togo]] announces the arrest of [[Burkina Faso]]'s former transitional [[President of Burkina Faso|president]] [[Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba]] in [[Lomé]] last week and expels him after Burkinabè officials accuse him of plotting attempted [[Coup d'état|coups]] and targeted assassinations against the [[Patriotic Movement for Safeguard and Restoration|ruling junta]]. [https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/19/01/2026/togo-expels-alleged-leader-of-burkina-fasos-foiled-coup-sources (AFP via ''The Peninsula'')]
*Four alleged [[Illegal drug trade|drug traffickers]] are fatally shot in an overnight [[shootout]] with border guards while crossing the [[Afghanistan–Tajikistan border]] into [[Tajikistan]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/afghan-gunman-killed-border-tajikistan-b2903121.html (''The Independent'')]
*A gunman shoots and kills one person and injures six others, before killing himself, in a [[mass shooting]] at the [[town hall]] of [[Chřibská]], [[Czech Republic]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/shooting-czech-town-hall-kills-one-shooter-also-dead-police-say-2026-01-19/ (Reuters)]
